title: Micronesia
capsule: The Federated States of Micronesia (FSM) comprises four states — Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, and Kosrae — spread across the Caroline Islands in the western Pacific. Previously administered under the U.S.-governed Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands, FSM entered into a Compact of Free Association with the United States in 1986 and joined the United Nations that year; the 1987 attested start in this dataset reflects the Compact's full operationalization. The Compact provides U.S. defense guarantees and financial transfers in exchange for U.S. military access rights; it was renewed in 2003 and again negotiated in the early 2020s. With limited land area and a dispersed population, FSM faces significant challenges from outmigration, subsistence-level outer-island economies, and rising sea levels threatening low-lying atolls.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Modern sovereign state with defined maritime boundaries; the island territories are precisely documented though the exclusive economic zone is vast.
